evals.prompt: Is interest in intermittent fasting growing among Polish- and Czech-language readers, and how much can we trust that trend? We're deciding whether to localize our fasting app.
evals.expected_output: Czech has an article, Polish has no linked intermittent-fasting article: reported as no data (not a niche), a broad 'Post' article not compared on size; trend judged against whole-wiki traffic and a control topic.
assertions: Judges the trend against overall Wikipedia traffic change (normalization) before calling interest falling or growing
Uses a control or comparison topic from the same field (e.g. Dieting)

Handles the Polish article gap correctly: says there is no same-concept Polish article (or uses one only for trend), never presents the gap or a broad 'Post'/fasting article size as low interest or a niche/opportunity
Every number in the answer comes from fetched Wikimedia data or is explicitly labelled as outside knowledge (no invented or hand-derived figures like monthly totals or user estimates)
States a confidence/trust level with concrete reasons (e.g. volume, trend consistency, spikes)
Refers to language audiences, not countries/markets (no 'Poland market', no country flags)
Produces a shareable report file (PDF) and a chart in the outputs folder
Ends with a concrete way to validate (attention is not demand)
